derived_from: The restored human-written Wisent corpus (wisent-landing-new@ff59cf6, live at ster.wisent.com/docs) — the writing exemplar
documentation-site-examples: 50 references + content-structure dataset (~941k URLs, 647-page anatomy)
note: Judgment layer only: these lines score qualities the mechanical validators cannot see (ordering, voice, framing, pairing). Claims, drift, terms, structure and coverage stay mechanical. Every line is binary: pass or fail.

lines.check: The overview page's first paragraph states the outcome the reader gets, not the implementation.
Within every page, sections are ordered general to specific.
Every code block appears before the prose that discusses it, never after.
Quick start is one linear paste-ready path that ends in one observable result, with no branching before that result.
Every task-guide slug and title names the reader's task (verb + object, e.g. 'Ship a release'), never a feature noun.
Every term declared in plan.terms is defined on its defining page, and pages that use the term appear after that defining page in nav order.
lines.source: guidelines terms rule; the 'fleet was never defined' defect

lines.check: Every cli-reference, api-reference, config-reference and sdk-reference entry follows the same anatomy in the same order (usage block, argument table, then variants/examples).
Enumerable facts — flags, defaults, error codes, limit values — appear in table blocks, never in running prose.
Callout blocks carry warnings, gotchas and tips only; primary instructions never hide inside a callout.
Every step-list item is one imperative action addressed to the reader.
No block contains marketing register — superlatives, hype adjectives, or claims about being fastest/best/most advanced.
Each page addresses one consistent reader level; beginner and advanced material are separate pages, not interleaved sections.
Guide-to-reference pointers name the target page's title explicitly in prose (the layout renders plain text; there are no inline links to rely on).
Security statements appear on the page of the surface they concern; nothing security-relevant is collected onto an arbitrary page.
Every limits block states concrete numbers with units and where each limit is set; no limit is described without its value.
Changelog entries describe user-visible changes only, one condensed bullet each, in the changelog's own section names.
Every removed-or-changed behavior mention pairs with what replaces it and what the reader should run instead; no orphan removals.
Support content, when present, comes last in the page order.
Optional kinds (faq, contributing, roadmap, versions) appear only where the plan's own claims provide sourced material for every entry.
Guide and concept titles state outcomes in corpus voice ('One queue, one registry, one answer.'); reference titles are plain noun phrases of the surface they document.
